items.canonicalSource: No canonical answer exists. Three self-consistent ratified positions collide: 24.08.01 D-01 ("Fully automatic on match: block, preserve, report, action — no human decision"); 24.02.03 Edge Cases ("Required Art 17 field empty at commit … the all-or-nothing unit is refused → **sanction never applies**") plus "Automated means contributed | Flag is mandatory and **honest**"; and trust-safety-disputes-cx.md CX-12 ("the enforcement record's user-facing reason field is deliberately generic — 24.02 must not leak a CSAM-specific reason into an SoR").
items.ownerBrief:
DECISION NEEDED — what the mandatory `facts-relied-on` field says on a fully automatic CSAM suspension, and what `concurrence` carries when no human was ever in the loop. This is counsel's call and it cannot be resolved from the tree, because none of the three positions is drift from the others.

THE COLLISION. A CSAM hash match applies the account sanction automatically with no human decision (24.08.01 D-01). Every sanction must land atomically with its Art 17 Statement of Reasons, and the SoR is generated — never typed — from a structured decision record whose required fields are validated: if `facts-relied-on` is empty, null or malformed at commit, generation fails, the all-or-nothing unit is refused, and the sanction never applies (24.02.03 Behavior + Edge Cases + D-04). The automated-means flag must be set and honest. Meanwhile CX-12's masking rule forbids the CSAM basis from reaching the subject in any form: they see only 24.02's generic suspension notice, and reinstatement runs the ordinary suspension-review path without the basis surfacing. So the field must simultaneously be non-empty, honest, and silent about the real reason. No file in the tree states wording that satisfies all three, and the implementer cannot invent it: too specific tips off a true offender and prejudices a live NCMEC referral; too vague is functionally a denial of the Art 20 appeal right (24.02.03's own Role Lens says exactly that of a vague facts field); and blank blocks the suspension entirely, which is the worst outcome available — a matched account that stays live because a notice field could not be filled.

THE SECOND, SHARPER HALF. The decision record's `concurrence` field is optional-with-a-reason over a CLOSED enum: a concurring reviewer ID, or `below-concurrence-threshold` (with a cooling-off re-affirmation timestamp), or `s0-s1-clock-override` (24.02.03 D-08; 24.02.01 D-07 as amended, D-09). Blank fails validation and blocks the sanction. Every value in that enum presupposes a human moderator who decided and then either got or did not get a second pair of eyes. A CSAM action has no moderator at all — 24.08 D-02 makes it structurally impossible for the material to reach any queue. `s0-s1-clock-override` is the closest fit and it is still wrong on its face: D-09 describes a rung ≥ 6 sanction applying 'on the single moderator's decision', and here there is no moderator's decision to apply. Either the enum gains a value for a fully automatic action, or the CSAM path is exempted from the concurrence field, or D-01's fully-automatic property is qualified. All three are product/legal decisions with different downstream consequences: the transparency projection (24.02.06 D-04) reads this field to describe the process the platform actually ran, so whatever is chosen becomes a public statement about how the platform enforces.

WHAT IS ALREADY FIXED AND NOT IN QUESTION: the action itself (block, preserve, report, action, automatically), the masking (never a CSAM-specific reason), the absence of a self-service appeal (D-06), and the reinstatement route (generic suspension review). Only the record-and-notice wording is open.

RECOMMENDED SHAPE OF AN ANSWER (the owner's to accept or replace): counsel approves a single fixed generic facts string tied to a named prohibited-content rule version — one that is literally true of the account action, discloses no detection capability, and is reused verbatim so that its presence is not itself a signal — and the concurrence enum gains one value for an action with no human decider, so the transparency report can state honestly how many actions were fully automatic. This preserves the atomic sanction⇔SoR guarantee without either lying in a statutory field or leaving a matched account live.

A tracked question has been written into the tree at 24.08.01 Q-05 (owner: User + counsel, deferred to `/create-prd-security`, reading with Q-04). Nothing else was changed — no wording was invented.
items.summary: Two owning files carry opposed, self-consistent ratified positions and the resolution changes what a sanctioned user is told, so this is the owner's. 24.08.01 D-01 requires a fully automatic action with no human; 24.02.03 requires every Art 17 field non-empty, validated and honest, refusing the sanction otherwise; CX-12 forbids the true basis appearing. Nothing states what wording satisfies all three, and the closed `concurrence` enum has no value describing an action no moderator touched. No fix applied; 24.08.01 Q-05 added as a tracked [OWNER] question (User + counsel, /create-prd-security).
